team_signals.summary: Arizona improved its line and installed Mike LaFleur's system, but expected quarterback regression could cap the passing-game volume available to its receivers.
team_signals.mechanism: Better design cannot fully offset weaker quarterback efficiency, reducing confidence in repeat target totals for the top pass catchers.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Arizona's rebuilt 2026 offensive line B-, improved on the left side but still thin and unsettled at right tackle.
team_signals.mechanism: An upgraded interior helps, while right-tackle and depth risk keep protection and run efficiency from being a clear strength.

team_signals.summary: Kevin Stefanski and elite line coach Bill Callahan bring a wide-zone plan expected to run through Bijan Robinson, with Kyle Pitts positioned for short-area work.
team_signals.mechanism: A stabilized line and scheme fit support high rushing efficiency and receiving access for the offense's two most important mismatch players.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Atlanta's 2026 line C+, with four credible starters but a major right-tackle question despite Bill Callahan's arrival.
team_signals.mechanism: Strong coaching and interior play can support the run, while one weak edge can still disrupt protection and outside concepts.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Baltimore's revamped 2026 line C- after losing center Tyler Linderbaum and changing three interior spots.
team_signals.mechanism: Interior turnover and a center downgrade can weaken both pocket stability and the run game until the new group gels.

team_signals.summary: Baltimore is installing a new run-first spread system with play action, creating upside but also a meaningful early-season learning curve.
team_signals.mechanism: The design fits Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry, and Zay Flowers, while a completely new staff and playbook make the timing and magnitude uncertain.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Buffalo's mostly intact 2026 line A after top-four pass- and run-blocking results in 2025.
team_signals.mechanism: Continuity and high-end blocking support both Josh Allen's pocket and the backfield's efficiency, with left guard the main uncertainty.

team_signals.summary: Buffalo remains a run-led, play-action offense with Josh Allen controlling checks and a stronger receiving group around him.
team_signals.mechanism: Continuity, a productive line, and clearer high-value roles support the primary Bills skill players, while complex option rules can punish receivers who do not earn Allen's trust.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Carolina's deep, balanced 2026 line B+ after a top-four run-blocking finish in 2025.
team_signals.mechanism: Solid starters and credible tackle depth should create running room and reduce the burden on the quarterback.

team_signals.summary: Carolina's slow, quick-pass offense supports its running backs and shallow-route receivers but remains vulnerable when defenses vary pressure against simple protection rules.
team_signals.mechanism: High-percentage throws and run volume create usable roles, while the protection design and Bryce Young's limited ceiling constrain explosive output.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Chicago's deep 2026 line A- after top-five pass- and run-blocking results and further draft investment.
team_signals.mechanism: Strong protection and run blocking increase the efficiency floor for Caleb Williams and the backfield.

team_signals.summary: Chicago returns Ben Johnson's versatile run-first offense with improved line depth and defined short-area and vertical roles.
team_signals.mechanism: The structure creates easier throws for Caleb Williams while preserving deep-shot upside and a productive rushing base.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Cincinnati's young, intact 2026 line C after bottom-seven pass- and run-blocking results in 2025.
team_signals.mechanism: Late-season growth offers hope, but continued tackle and youth-related inconsistency can pressure the quarterback and limit rushing efficiency.

team_signals.summary: Cincinnati retains a concentrated, quick-game passing attack built around Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and defined red-zone roles.
team_signals.mechanism: Continuity and concentrated opportunity make the core Bengals options comparatively dependable even though the offense plays slower than its reputation suggests.

team_signals.summary: Cleveland enters a rebuild with an unsettled multi-quarterback plan and a new staff that may struggle to establish a stable passing hierarchy.
team_signals.mechanism: Quarterback changes can disrupt timing, target quality, and weekly receiver roles, creating unusually high redraft volatility.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Cleveland's overhauled 2026 line D after it finished last in pass blocking and near the bottom in run blocking in 2025.
team_signals.mechanism: Five-man turnover may eventually help, but weak recent performance and cohesion risk materially lower early-season confidence.

team_signals.summary: Dallas retains a fast, pass-heavy offense with two dangerous receivers and an improved, scheme-versatile line supporting a high-snap lead back.
team_signals.mechanism: Pace and concentrated high-value roles support CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Javonte Williams even if raw rushing volume is modest.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Dallas' 2026 line C: strong interior run blocking but continued problems at both tackle spots.
team_signals.mechanism: The split profile supports the rushing lane efficiency while leaving the passing game exposed to edge pressure.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Denver's intact 2026 line A+, calling it arguably the league's best after elite protection in 2025.
team_signals.mechanism: Five returning starters and strong depth raise both pocket stability and rushing efficiency.

team_signals.summary: Sean Payton's offense remains productive but unusually difficult to project outside quarterback because weekly personnel usage changes frequently.
team_signals.mechanism: The scheme can create efficient touches, but volatile snap and touch allocation lowers confidence in secondary Denver skill players.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Detroit's diminished 2026 line C, with run blocking still stronger than protection.
team_signals.mechanism: A weaker interior and reliance on a rookie lower Jared Goff's protection floor, while the run game can remain useful if the unit stays healthy.

team_signals.summary: Detroit's new coordinator is expected to feature Jahmyr Gibbs and use a rhythm passing game that emphasizes Amon-Ra St. Brown and Sam LaPorta over the middle.
team_signals.mechanism: Concentrated touches and a coordinator history favorable to tight ends support the primary Lions options, though Jared Goff must adapt to added control at the line.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Green Bay's 2026 line D and identifies the interior as one of the league's weakest groups.
team_signals.mechanism: Interior pressure and limited rushing lanes can hurt Jordan Love's efficiency and Josh Jacobs' aging rushing profile.

team_signals.summary: Green Bay reduced its receiver rotation but still projects Christian Watson and Jayden Reed into different specialized roles rather than one dominant target funnel.
team_signals.mechanism: Fewer bodies help, yet role specialization can keep weekly volume uneven and makes the hierarchy important to monitor.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Houston's still-changing 2026 line C after below-average protection and run blocking in 2025.
team_signals.mechanism: A rookie center, young tackle, and injury-prone veterans create a wide outcome range and continued pressure risk for C.J. Stroud.

team_signals.summary: Houston projects David Montgomery for lead and red-zone work, with Woody Marks serving more as a change-of-pace receiver.
team_signals.mechanism: Early-down and goal-line volume is particularly useful in non-PPR scoring and can sustain value without a dominant receiving share.

team_signals.summary: Houston's offense remains conservative and matchup-driven despite having receivers capable of winning downfield.
team_signals.mechanism: If the staff continues to prioritize avoiding mistakes over aggression, C.J. Stroud and the vertical receivers may have less passing volume and ceiling than their talent implies.

team_signals.summary: Indianapolis lost a starting tackle and its boundary target while relying on Daniel Jones after several major injuries.
team_signals.mechanism: Weaker protection, less formation-defining receiver gravity, and quarterback durability uncertainty lower the stability of the offense around Jonathan Taylor and the wideouts.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Indianapolis' mostly intact 2026 line A after top-four pass- and run-blocking results in 2025.
team_signals.mechanism: High-end blocking supports Jonathan Taylor and the passing game, with a young new right tackle the primary risk.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Jacksonville's returning 2026 line C after solid but uneven 2025 results and persistent sack problems.
team_signals.mechanism: Continuity helps timing, but tackle pressure keeps the offense from receiving a positive line adjustment.

team_signals.summary: Jacksonville's staff sees Bhayshul Tuten in the lead role, with Chris Rodriguez carrying direct contingency and red-zone value.
team_signals.mechanism: A productive scheme and defined handcuff path create upside, but Tuten's ball security remains a role risk.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Kansas City's 2026 line B-, with credible blocking but several changed starters and health questions.
team_signals.mechanism: The unit is slightly above average on paper but not strong enough to erase early uncertainty around the rebuilt offense.

team_signals.summary: Kansas City rebuilt around a stronger run game and expects to lean on it while Patrick Mahomes completes his return from an ACL injury.
team_signals.mechanism: Early rushing volume and Kenneth Walker's all-purpose fit raise the value of the backfield, though the balance may change as Mahomes regains full confidence.

team_signals.summary: The Chargers lost starting center Tyler Biadasz to season-ending injured reserve with a knee injury.
team_signals.mechanism: The confirmed loss weakens interior pass protection and run-blocking continuity, creating a modest downside adjustment for the quarterback and running-back environment.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Las Vegas' 2026 line C after last-place sack and adjusted-line-yard results, with the new staff expected to improve the scheme.
team_signals.mechanism: Coaching can help, but the prior baseline and personnel questions still create pressure and rushing-efficiency risk.

team_signals.summary: Klint Kubiak and Rick Dennison bring a proven system that is expected to feature Ashton Jeanty and use Brock Bowers as the primary movable mismatch.
team_signals.mechanism: Concentrated roles in a run-led, play-action structure support both cornerstone players even if wide receiver volume stays limited.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades the healthier, reinforced Chargers line A and sees top-10 potential under the new staff.
team_signals.mechanism: Improved personnel, coaching, and fullback support materially strengthen the environment for Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton.

team_signals.summary: Mike McDaniel joins Jim Harbaugh with added blockers and a plan centered on Omarion Hampton while reducing the need for Justin Herbert to run.
team_signals.mechanism: The line and run design strongly support Hampton; better protection helps Herbert, but fewer designed scrambles can offset some quarterback upside.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades the Rams' 2026 line A- after it led the league in run blocking and adjusted line yards in 2025.
team_signals.mechanism: Elite run blocking supports Kyren Williams, though thin depth and a possible suspension create some fragility.

team_signals.summary: The Rams retain Sean McVay's concentrated, proven offense with tight formations supporting quick receivers and Kyren Williams holding the high-value backfield work.
team_signals.mechanism: Continuity and clearly assigned passing-down, goal-line, and primary receiving roles improve projection stability for the core players.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Miami's largely unchanged 2026 line D after bottom-six pass- and run-blocking results in 2025.
team_signals.mechanism: A weak line can undermine the new run-first plan and lower both quarterback efficiency and backfield consistency.

team_signals.summary: Miami's rebuilt staff still plans to center the offense on De'Von Achane in both the run and short passing games.
team_signals.mechanism: Wide-zone volume and a large receiving role provide multiple paths to production even if game script or the passing personnel disappoints.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Minnesota's 2026 line C, with capable tackles but a questionable interior and a new line coach.
team_signals.mechanism: Edge protection may hold up, while interior weakness creates more concern for the run game and quarterback durability.

team_signals.summary: Minnesota's offense remains pass-led and concentrated around Justin Jefferson, with short play-action concepts also supporting T.J. Hockenson.
team_signals.mechanism: The target funnel protects the primary pass catchers from some of the uncertainty created by a possible multi-quarterback season.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades New England's talented 2026 line B+, with high upside if its young tackles and injury-prone veterans stay available.
team_signals.mechanism: Improved protection and depth support Drake Maye and the run game, but health and position changes still create variance.

team_signals.summary: New England's motion, RPO, and play-action structure gives Drake Maye clearer reads and now pairs him with a deeper receiving group.
team_signals.mechanism: Improved weapons and designed rushing can raise the quarterback ceiling, though Maye's tendency to distribute targets limits confidence in any one secondary receiver.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades New Orleans' 2026 line C, with a decent left side but weak run blocking and unresolved right-side questions.
team_signals.mechanism: Average protection may be serviceable, but limited rushing lanes reduce confidence in the backfield exceeding its role-based value.

team_signals.summary: New Orleans upgraded its weak line spot and added explosive runners and receivers to a flexible Kellen Moore offense.
team_signals.mechanism: Better protection and more explosive personnel open space for Travis Etienne and Chris Olave, though the ceiling still depends on Tyler Shough taking a second-year step.

team_signals.summary: New York's new staff upgraded the line and plans a high-volume RPO run game with Isaiah Likely in a prominent quick-read role.
team_signals.mechanism: Better protection and defined RPO answers support Jaxson Dart and Likely, although the offense still must prove the transition works in games.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades the improved Giants line C+, with new guard talent and experienced depth but no top-tier projection.
team_signals.mechanism: The group should be serviceable enough to help Jaxson Dart and the run game, but it is not a distinct fantasy advantage.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades the Jets' 2026 line C- after guard losses and continued center and cohesion questions.
team_signals.mechanism: Promising young tackles cannot fully offset interior weakness, lowering confidence in both protection and run efficiency.

team_signals.summary: The Jets have publicly discussed splitting backfield touches among three runners despite Breece Hall being the most dangerous option.
team_signals.mechanism: A real three-way rotation would reduce Hall's snap and touch ceiling, but the coaching plan is not yet proven in regular-season usage.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Philadelphia's 2026 line B+, still strong and younger despite a coaching change and some recent injuries.
team_signals.mechanism: Above-average line play supports the run-led offense, though the group is no longer the automatic league-best unit of prior seasons.

team_signals.summary: Philadelphia's new passing identity is expected to attack intermediate areas more often after A.J. Brown's departure, concentrating opportunity around DeVonta Smith.
team_signals.mechanism: A clearer lead role and route emphasis that fits Smith can raise both target share and weekly consistency.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Pittsburgh's young, improving 2026 line B after a strong pass-blocking season and further first-round investment.
team_signals.mechanism: An upward-trending unit improves the floor for the quarterback and backfield, with health the main unresolved issue.

team_signals.summary: Mike McCarthy's offense projects Jaylen Warren for passing-down work while Rico Dowdle handles more early-down and goal-line snaps.
team_signals.mechanism: Aaron Rodgers' recent tendency to target running backs gives Warren a useful receiving path, though the split limits the ceiling of both backs.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades San Francisco's 2026 line B, with strong tackle play and run blocking but one weak interior spot and age-related fragility.
team_signals.mechanism: The unit remains a net positive when healthy, though Trent Williams' availability materially affects the outlook.

team_signals.summary: San Francisco continues to evolve its short, run-led offense and added personnel that may reopen more deep opportunities for Brock Purdy.
team_signals.mechanism: Kyle Shanahan's interchangeable formations sustain efficiency while the new vertical threats add ceiling without replacing the established underneath roles.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Seattle's 2026 line C and expects regression after losing the coaches who helped mask weak guard play.
team_signals.mechanism: A first-time play caller and weaker line instruction increase pressure and rushing-efficiency risk despite some young depth.

team_signals.summary: Seattle lost the coaches who drove its title offense and now relies on a first-time play caller while replacing its lead runner without a clear second receiver.
team_signals.mechanism: Similar early concepts may mask the transition, but weaker week-to-week adjustment, rushing efficiency, and target support create regression risk.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Tampa Bay's 2026 line C+, with strong tackles but interior and depth questions.
team_signals.mechanism: The unit is close to neutral: healthy starters can improve it, but the interior does not justify a positive fantasy adjustment yet.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru questions Baker Mayfield's fit in Zac Robinson's shotgun- and pistol-heavy offense.
team_signals.mechanism: A scheme mismatch can reduce efficiency and timing even if Mayfield's competitiveness preserves volume and job security.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Tennessee's 2026 offensive line D-, one of the league's worst units despite a new coach and several additions.
team_signals.mechanism: Weak depth and multiple underperforming starters can derail Cam Ward's development and prevent the new run scheme from creating consistent lanes.

team_signals.summary: Tennessee replaced its staff with Robert Saleh, Brian Daboll, and a new line coach, installing a run-first offense built on horizontal spacing, quick throws, RPOs, and play action.
team_signals.mechanism: The design could make reads easier for Cam Ward and create clearer receiver roles, but the entire projection depends on Ward's development and the line executing a changed blocking mix.

team_signals.summary: FantasyGuru grades Washington's 2026 line C-, with two strong pieces but continued interior holes.
team_signals.mechanism: Inconsistent inside blocking raises durability and efficiency concerns for Jayden Daniels and the run game.

team_signals.summary: Washington handed its offense to first-time coordinator David Blough, with broad player freedom but little evidence yet that the many concepts will form a coherent system.
team_signals.mechanism: The talent and tempo create upside, while play-calling inexperience and uncertain role integration raise execution risk.
